name: Ptah-hotep
credit: The Prisse Papyrus (Middle Kingdom; Bibliothèque nationale de France), a detail from the Instruction of Kagemni, which precedes the Instruction of Ptah-hotep on the roll · An artifact, shown because no authentic portrait exists · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Ptah-hotep is the vizier of King Isesi of the Fifth Dynasty of Egypt, the traditional author of the wisdom text known as the Instruction of Ptah-hotep. In it an aged vizier, feeling the weight of his years, asks the king for leave to pass his office to his son, and sets down for him a series of maxims on speech, manners, justice and the conduct of a good official.

The text survives chiefly in the Prisse Papyrus, now in the Bibliothèque nationale in Paris, which dates from the Middle Kingdom, many centuries after the vizier is said to have lived. The attribution to Ptah-hotep is traditional, and the date given here is the traditional one.
